solution:
Use $\cos^2 x = \tfrac12(1+\cos 2x)$:
$$\int_0^{\pi/2} \cos^2 x\,dx = \frac12\int_0^{\pi/2} (1+\cos 2x)\,dx = \frac12\Bigl[x + \tfrac12\sin 2x\Bigr]_0^{\pi/2}.$$
At $x=\tfrac{\pi}{2}$, $\sin\pi=0$; at $x=0$, both terms vanish. Hence
$$\int_0^{\pi/2} \cos^2 x\,dx = \frac12\cdot\frac{\pi}{2} = \frac{\pi}{4}.$$
(By symmetry $\int_0^{\pi/2}\sin^2 x\,dx=\tfrac{\pi}{4}$ also.)
